races.name: QuinnBet Apprentice Optional Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with modest recent form (3-0-8-6-2), proven on good going but operating out of her deepest hold-up role in a field this crowded; blinkers fitted and the 12-day turnaround is sharp, but the redistribution to midfield does not suit a horse who needs to come late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts but shaped with promise last time, finishing second twelve days ago to arrive here in decent nick; she has run over today's trip and going before, though her ranking of sixth from eleven in the field suggests she faces a stiff task from stall six carrying 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Kakori
runners_data.note: Returned from a 69-day break which is a significant concern, last won in Listed company over further and the step back to 10f is untested at this level; a genuine hold-up type who will find the likely steady pace an obstacle, and the long absence makes confidence hard to justify.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 69 days off, Kakori has going experience to call on but faces a stiff ask from stall ten carrying 142 lb; third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement, though consistency remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Loingseoir
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran who has placed on good ground nine times in 15 similar-going runs and was fourth over 10f on good ground recently — the trip and conditions suit, and the hold-up style is his natural groove, making him one of the more reliable closers if a run materialises.
runners_data.comment: Loingseoir arrives here third last time out and brings strong claims on our rating, which puts him narrowly top of the rankings; he has run over today's trip and going, and from stall three carries 142 lb, though the main concern is that he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Phidias Ovation
runners_data.note: Modest OR of 53 and a 67-day break, with the flagged fade-in-finish concern reinforcing that this horse struggles to sustain any effort; operates in hold-up fashion and even redistributed to midfield, the finishing tendency makes victory hard to construct.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Phidias Ovation arrives 67 days since his last outing and faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's going before and that experience offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Bucaneer's Spirit
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with good-ground form (12 of 15 runs on similar going) and a 1W4P record in that company, including a second over 8f recently; true hold-up type placed in midfield on the map, and the packed rear group means getting a clean run through will be the decisive factor.
runners_data.comment: Bucaneer's Spirit shaped well for a podium finish three starts back and brings solid distance-and-going experience to the table, with our rating of 74 putting him ahead of his official mark; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and a return to form is needed.

runners_data.name: Kashel Spring
runners_data.note: Rated 73 and the joint-highest in the field, but the last two runs were over 16f on very different ground and the step back to 10f is a significant drop in trip; apprentice claimer Mel Sheridan takes 7lbs off, and the hold-up style is genuine, though recent course form does not encourage.
runners_data.comment: Kashel Spring arrives here in fair trim — a winner four starts back and though only fifth and sixth in more recent outings, with experience of both today's trip and going working in her favour from stall 8. The main concern is trainer form, currently just 1 from 24 over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, won over 10f on good ground 11 days ago at the same course, and with no pace rival she should lead in full control; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that she is primarily a lead type who may be vulnerable late, but the track and conditions are familiar.
runners_data.comment: Hexagonal landed a win three starts back but has been out of the frame in his two most recent outings, and a trainer strike-rate of just 4% over the past fortnight is a concern, though the quick 11-day turnaround and experience over today's trip and going offer some positives.

runners_data.name: Concert Party
runners_data.note: A four-year-old from the Hogan yard who is a natural hold-up horse despite a prominent map position; 13-day turnaround and the form string (1-0-9-5-0) is modest, with the best run a win over 10f that matches today's trip, but good-ground record of 0W0P is not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Fifth two starts back hints at some ability, but Concert Party has been largely out of the frame in recent starts and her trainer is in a lean spell at 1/24 over the last fortnight; the experience over today's trip and going gives some grounding, though her overall form makes faith tricky.

runners_data.name: Forlio
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on good ground just 10 days ago for Paul Flynn, which is the most relevant and recent piece of form in this field; the hold-up style is genuine and maps well given the trip extension, and the blinkers have been a positive influence on a horse whose good-ground record reads 2W3P.
runners_data.comment: Forlio won two starts back and returns here fit on just ten days' rest, with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour. He carries 126 lb from stall one, and though his trainer is in a quiet spell, his overall profile makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Moyassr
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground and the trip is spot-on, but the form string ends in three zeros and the redistributed midfield position does not play to a horse who needs to come from off the pace; the Flynn yard has had no winners in the last 14 days, adding to the caution.
runners_data.comment: Moyassr has been unplaced in each of his last two starts and, with his trainer yet to score in 27 attempts over the past fortnight, confidence is hard to find; he has run over today's trip and going before, but that does little to offset a ranking of ninth from eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: She's Ideal
runners_data.note: Back in six days from a win over 10f on good ground, making her the freshest and most in-form prominent runner in the race; Adrian McGuinness has five winners from 28 runners in the past 14 days, the trip matches her winning distance, and the prominent style means she will not be inconvenienced by the likely gentle pace.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, She's Ideal faces a stiff ask here, though back-to-back wins in her last two starts give her genuine current form to cling to; she has experience over today's trip and going, and 126 lb from stall five is her lot.

races.paceDynamic: Hexagonal is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine rival for the early lead, she should coast to the front and dictate a controlled, even gallop over this flat 1m2½f trip on good ground. She's Ideal and Concert Party are mapped prominent but their natural style leans hold-up, meaning Hexagonal will very likely lead in isolation with a small group tracking at a respectful distance. The bulk of the 11-runner field — Darkdeserthighway, Kakori, Bucaneer's Spirit, Phidias Ovation, Concert Party and Moyassr — are all genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because more closers exist than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; in practice, several will jostle for the same rear-group position and not all will settle where they wish. A sustainable, uncontested pace set by Hexagonal over a flat circuit strongly favours horses who can track in second or third and kick from a prominent position, rather than deep closers who need a truly searching gallop to make up ground late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hexagonal Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hexagonal leads without pressure and the pace remains honest but controlled throughout.
scenarios.body: Hexagonal bowls along at a measured tempo, and the race becomes a test of who can quicken from a tracking position turning in; horses who travel prominently without burning energy early are perfectly set up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tucked in second or third cruises into the straight and overwhelms a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: The controlled early pace means the front two or three travel well within themselves and the lead swaps hands turning for home as Hexagonal's effort flattens out; a well-positioned tracker with a strong recent run has the clearest route.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely fast enough to string the field out and create a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Despite Hexagonal's expected restraint, a large 11-runner field on a tight circuit can create scrimmaging that produces a clear late run; Forlio, who won over 12f on good ground recently, or Bucaneer's Spirit with good-ground form could benefit if the gaps come.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos In Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Hexagonal sets a falsely slow early pace that bunches the field and produces a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A blanket field turning in together would favour a horse with a sharp turn of foot, but most of these runners are stayers or grinders rather than sprinters; a muddled finish is the least likely outcome given Hexagonal's course-winning profile and the clear leader advantage.

watchPoints.text: Hexagonal holds all the pace cards — if she is allowed to bowl clear unchallenged early, she may prove very difficult to reel in on this flat track; watch for any rival who attempts to pressure her from the first furlong, as that would fundamentally alter the race shape.

She's Ideal returns just six days after her last win and her handler McGuinness is in sharp form; if she travels smoothly in the slipstream of Hexagonal rather than being niggled at in a bunched group, she becomes the most dangerous horse in the field.

Forlio's 12f win 10 days ago on good ground is the standout piece of recent form, but as a genuine hold-up type in a field full of closers, getting a clear run through a 11-runner field turning for home is not guaranteed — watch the inside rail draw.

Kakori's 69-day absence for Joseph O'Brien is worth monitoring in the market; horses returning from breaks of over eight weeks in apprentice claiming company at Roscommon can run creditably fresh, and the OR of 67 gives him a legitimate weight chance if fit.

The Hogan yard saddles three runners (Kashel Spring, Hexagonal, Concert Party) — watch for any intra-stable tactics, particularly whether Concert Party or Kashel Spring are ridden to assist Hexagonal by taking up positions that shield her from any challenge early.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Captain James Cook
runners_data.note: Trainer Aidan O'Brien second-string angle but Wayne Lordan retains the ride; both runs at 6f on good ground, stepping up to 7½f here for the first time which represents an obvious query, though form figures of 7 and 0 are modest and this trip extension is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Eighteenth Smiles
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for Joseph O'Brien and this horse has shown hints of ability (placed fifth three times) over 6–7f; its natural inclination is to come from off the pace but with the field stacked with hold-up horses the map pushes it into midfield, meaning it won't get the space it needs to produce its best.

runners_data.name: Hypiradon
runners_data.note: Running in Coleman's yard alongside Matavai Bay; both starts on good ground and over 7–7½f, yet form figures of 6 and 10 offer little encouragement, and the hold-up style in a pace-light race makes a winning run difficult to envisage without significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Nando Royale
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and likely to lead unchallenged for Gary Carroll and Gavin Cromwell; posted a placed run over 8f on good ground which is relevant experience, and his ability to control the tempo without a rival pressing him is the pivotal tactical factor shaping this entire race.

runners_data.name: Pints Of Glory
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners this GM Lyons runner, which is the standout jockey-trainer combination for a hold-up horse in this field; ran 4th over 8f most recently which demonstrates some ability, though the likely controlled gallop set by a lone front-runner means late closers face a stiff task finding the necessary momentum.

runners_data.name: Prince Of Peppard
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh-trained juvenile with headgear noted; two starts at 6f on good ground with form of 6 and 9 are unencouraging, and the hold-up style suits this race least of all with the pace likely to be manageable throughout.

runners_data.name: Cashel Queen
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien runner with the most solid form in the field — placed in all three starts including a second over 8f — and a 5lb apprentice claim for Paddy Harnett softens the weight; her natural racing style is to come from behind, and while the map places her in midfield due to the crowded rear, her form at the trip gives her a genuine each-way profile if she threads through.

runners_data.name: Green Sparkle
runners_data.note: Flags a tendency to fade in the closing stages, which is a concern in any scenario; Joseph O'Brien sends this one out again quickly (9 days) and while the trainer strike rate is formidable, back-to-back blanks of 9 and 10 at 7f on good ground make it hard to make a case — the redistribution to midfield rather than its preferred off-the-pace berth only adds to the tactical difficulty.

runners_data.name: Honey Deuce
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan rides for small trainer JA Stack who has had no winners in the last 14 days; two starts at 7f with a best of 6th suggest modest ability, and as a hold-up horse in a controlled-pace maiden this runner looks likely to find things happening too quickly for it in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Luca Brillante
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld sends out this lightly-raced juvenile after just 9 days rest with an unknown running style (U flag) and only two starts at 6f; the step up in trip is uncharted territory, but Weld's training of improving juveniles is always worth noting even if the form reads 6 and 7.

runners_data.name: Matavai Bay
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides this second Coleman runner and the prominent style suits the anticipated race shape well; form of 6 at 6f and 10 at 7f is modest, but racing close to the pace in a slowly-run maiden gives it every opportunity to outrun its marks if it has improved since those runs.

runners_data.name: Someday Somewhere
runners_data.note: Willie Lee partners this Stephen Thorne-trained runner with an unknown style but consistent placed form (4th and 3rd) across 6–7f on good ground; the trip and going are familiar territory and the progressive profile relative to rivals with no wins between them makes this one of the more interesting unexposed quantities in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Nando Royale is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner maiden and should stride to the lead unchallenged from the off, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over 7½ furlongs on good ground at Roscommon. With no other genuine lead type in the field to press or test him, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, creating a scenario where those tracking him in the slipstream — Captain James Cook, Matavai Bay — are ideally placed to pounce. The lack of genuine pace pressure means closers will need to cover ground late from further back, a task complicated by a flat course but possible on good going if the early tempo is genuinely slow. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit a length or two off Nando Royale and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out — front-proximity is the winning profile here. Note that the field contains more true hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Eighteenth Smiles, Cashel Queen, and Green Sparkle are genuine off-the-pace types forced into midfield positions on the map, making it unlikely any of them secures their most effective running position in this pace-light shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Proximity Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Nando Royale bowls along in front at a steady-to-moderate clip and the race develops into a tactical contest from halfway.
scenarios.body: Nando Royale dictates on his own terms through the early stages and those immediately tracking him — Captain James Cook and Matavai Bay — are best positioned to launch their challenge two furlongs out without having to make up ground; a steady pace plays directly into the hands of horses racing in the first three or four.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Prominent Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the pace lifts significantly from halfway and those prominent types prove their stamina over the extra yardage of 7½ furlongs.
scenarios.body: A genuine increase in tempo from the home turn stretches the field and rewards horses with the class and fitness to sustain their effort under pressure, filtering out those who have merely been carried along by a slow gallop; Captain James Cook and Someday Somewhere, both showing progressive form figures, look the types to find reserves when the race genuinely develops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough early to string the field out and create a closing opportunity for those held up.
scenarios.body: In this shape the pace would need to be far stronger than the lone front-runner Nando Royale is likely to generate alone, making this scenario dependent on something unexpected raising the tempo considerably; Eighteenth Smiles and Pints Of Glory are the truest hold-up performers, but both are effectively racing out of their optimal position in this pace-light context, reducing their chance materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches mid-race, causing interference that disrupts the principals and opens a gap for a longer-priced runner.
scenarios.body: With 12 juveniles on a flat, turning track and several horses redistributed from their natural positions, traffic and interference through the turn is a genuine possibility that can hand an unexpected runner a clear passage at the right moment; Cashel Queen's placed form at the trip and Someday Somewhere's consistent record suggest they could capitalise if the race falls apart for the fancied runners.

watchPoints.text: Nando Royale holds all the pace cards here — if Gary Carroll gets a soft lead and the gallop is truly uncontested, any prominent horse that tracks within a length of him into the straight is in a commanding position that could prove insurmountable.

Cashel Queen's placed record (2nd, 3rd, 4th) over this trip and further gives her a clear form edge over most rivals, but Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim and the tactical compromise of not getting her natural hold-up position could see her finish with running left — watch for a late rattle without quite getting there.

With 12 two-year-olds going into the first bend at Roscommon, watch for crowding and positional scrimmaging in the early stages — Green Sparkle, Eighteenth Smiles and Prince Of Peppard are all hold-up types squeezed into midfield slots, increasing the chance of traffic issues mid-race.

Someday Somewhere and Luca Brillante are both unquantified style-wise (U flag) and lightly raced — if either breaks smartly and takes up a prominent position rather than dropping in, the pace dynamic shifts and the race could develop with more genuine competition for Nando Royale than expected.

Pints Of Glory (Colin Keane, GM Lyons) is the classiest jockey-trainer pairing among the hold-up contingent — if the pace does lift significantly entering the home straight, Keane's positional intelligence could see this one produce a strong late run that complicates the finish.

races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Race

runners_data.name: Seven Nation Army
runners_data.note: Front-runner for O'Brien who won at 7f on Soft but has been below par at 6f on Good recently; the step back to front-running duties over 7½f suits, though a contested lead with Sword Of State may find him out before the line.
runners_data.comment: Seven Nation Army arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, clocking up a sharp sequence that marks him out as a genuine threat; the risk is that our rating suggests he may be flattered by his official mark.

runners_data.name: Green Dreamer
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good and finished fifth at the same trip, giving him the best distance profile in the field; McMonagle's booking for O'Brien in a race they also run Seven Nation Army speaks to confidence, and a prominent-but-not-leading position suits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Green Dreamer arrives on the back of a win last time out and has already sampled today's trip and conditions, giving him a solid fitness and experience platform; the main risk is that his speed rating of 54 leaves him with plenty to prove against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Noble Agenda
runners_data.note: Sole run was a 7f win on Soft for Ciaran Murphy, so the Good ground is a slight unknown; the step up from one run is bold but Ben Coen's experience and a high OR of 120 suggest stable confidence, with 60 days off needing to be discounted slightly.
runners_data.comment: Noble Agenda arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, though 60 days off the track raises a fitness question; carrying 134 lb from stall 6, he has the profile of an each-way contender rather than a certainty, rated fifth of nine.

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced sort who wants to race prominently but has not won beyond 5f and has mixed results at 6f on Good; stepping up sharply in trip and class here, and the crowded early exchanges may cost him the position he needs.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and a winner five starts back, Lars Soldier brings solid recent form and going experience to this, and his rating of 92 marks him out as the one to beat in a field of nine; the 130 lb burden is the sole query.

runners_data.name: Oristown Boy
runners_data.note: Holds-up for effect and won over 7f on Good last time, which is the strongest recent form angle; Murray's small yard has had no recent winners but the horse's profile fits the expected race shape, tempered by the 5-runner hold-up sample showing fade tendencies.
runners_data.comment: Oristown Boy won last time out but his profile is undermined by a substantial gap between his official mark and our rating, leaving him ranked towards the foot of this field; he has run over today's trip and going, and comes here on a quick turnaround of sixteen days.

runners_data.name: Emotional Hedging
runners_data.note: Finished second on debut over 6f on Good for Cromwell and Carroll, a reliable combination; moves up significantly in trip to 7½f for only the second start, and whether she stays the extra distance is the key question in a prominent role.
runners_data.comment: Emotional Hedging shaped well when second last time out and returns on a quick turnaround of just 13 days, suggesting connections are keen, but his rating of 69 ranks him sixth of nine and he is yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Grit And Glory
runners_data.note: Finished last on debut over 7f on Good and is tagged with a fade flag; McAteer and Foley have modest recent strike rates, and with no positives beyond debut experience, this horse needs significant improvement to feature.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and rated well below the top of the field, Grit And Glory faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns reasonably fresh after a 33-day break from stall two carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Sword Of State
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good most recently and shapes as one of two confirmed front-runners; Rory Cleary's booking is positive and the course-distance form is relevant, but a head-to-head pace battle with Seven Nation Army from the gates is the central risk to its chance.
runners_data.comment: Sword Of State arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid profile at 127 lb from stall 3; the risk is that seventh two starts back hints her form can be inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Gabby Hayes
runners_data.note: Finished ninth on sole start over 7f on Good and carries a fade flag that undermines the hold-up profile; Noel Meade's yard has had no recent winners and with just one run to assess, this represents a significant step into the unknown.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Gabby Hayes faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip before and a 16-day turnaround suggests he is fit, but little else in the profile encourages confidence from stall one carrying 125 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Sword Of State and Seven Nation Army are both confirmed front-runners, setting up a genuine pace duel from the gates over this 7½f trip at Roscommon on Good ground. With four of nine runners wanting prominent ground — Lars Soldier and Emotional Hedging also pressing forward — there will be congestion in the early stages and a real fight to establish positions heading into the first bend, creating an honest, pressured gallop rather than a manufactured one. The contested pace duel between Sword Of State and Seven Nation Army means neither is likely to get a soft lead, and the sustained pressure through the middle portion of the race will test their reserves late. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and midfield horses who can track the pace battle from a comfortable position and pounce when the leaders tie each other up in the final two furlongs — Oristown Boy and Gabby Hayes are the natural profile beneficiaries, though the fade flags on both temper that verdict.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Sword Of State and Seven Nation Army fight for supremacy early and sustain an honest gallop that drains the front two entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The contested lead creates a true test that suits horses coming from midfield or off the pace who have been shielded from the battle, with the closing stages opening up for a strong finisher to swoop; Green Dreamer and Noble Agenda, sitting prominently but not in the scrap, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Sword Of State — asserts early dominance and the other yields, allowing a controlled, unchallenged gallop.
scenarios.body: A single pace-setter at a sensible rhythm on Good ground over 7½f can conserve enough energy to repel challenges late, particularly if the field is slow to organise behind; Sword Of State's recent 7f win on Good gives it the profile to hold on if gifted a soft lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest but not brutal, allowing a prominent tracker sitting just off the leaders to produce a timely challenge from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Lars Soldier and Emotional Hedging are in the firing line to benefit if they can avoid the early crowding and settle just behind the lead pair without being dragged into the duel; this is a credible shape on Good ground where stamina holds and tactical acuity matters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners truly burn each other out and the race collapses into a driving finish with the whole field converging from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Oristown Boy has the hold-up profile and a recent 7f win on Good to suggest genuine stamina, but both flagged closers carry fade concerns that reduce confidence in this shape truly delivering; this scenario requires a faster-than-expected early pace and clean passage through traffic.

watchPoints.text: Seven Nation Army and Sword Of State — watch the opening furlong to see which, if either, blinks first in the pace duel; if neither concedes, the early fractions will be sharp and the front two may be cooked by the 2f pole.

Lars Soldier and Emotional Hedging — four prominent-biased runners chasing two positions creates a real traffic risk between the 3f and 2f marks where the pace begins to consolidate; any runner caught wide or flat-footed here loses their chance.

Noble Agenda — 60 days off the track with just one career run means fitness is unproven; watch the pre-race paddock behaviour and how quickly Ben Coen can get him settled, as a fresh two-year-old at this class level can unravel quickly.

Oristown Boy — the hold-up profile only pays off if the pace is genuinely strong; if Sword Of State gets a soft lead and the gallop is falsely run, Oristown Boy will find himself with too much ground to make up on Good ground with no cut in it.

races.name: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
WTW Willis Handicap

runners_data.name: Engines On
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-pin, 65 days off the track which is a slight concern for sharpness, but goes well fresh; prominent racer who handles good ground well (9/15 on similar going) and Chris Hayes booking adds confidence — will attempt to sit just behind the leaders and pounce.
runners_data.comment: Engines On showed he can win at this level when scoring four starts back, but three unplaced efforts since then cast doubt on whether he has recaptured that form; 65 days off adds further uncertainty, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Summer Island
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for Lupini, just nine days after a run so likely cherry ripe; hold-up profile with an excellent record on good (9/15, two wins) and proven at 7f, making this hold-up shape ideal if the front-runners detonate.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Summer Island faces a stiff task from stall 17 carrying 139 lb, and that fifth last time out does little to inspire confidence; the saving graces are his experience over today's trip and going, and a winner twice in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Earls
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old but extraordinarily consistent, placing third or second in his last four starts over 8f on good ground; races prominently with tongue-tie and blinkers, Gary Carroll knows the horse well, and stepping back to 7½f may sharpen him up at a track he handles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Earls has been consistently close — second three of his last four completed efforts and third last time out — and he has experience over today's trip and conditions, but at 138 lb from stall 3, he faces a stiff ask to finally go one better.

runners_data.name: Spodo Komodo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 6f on soft and was placed over 7f good — the key question is whether he can sustain his pace when two other genuine leaders press him; Ronan Whelan will need to judge early fractions precisely or this horse will be a spent force before the two-furlong pole.
runners_data.comment: Spodo Komodo showed his quality with a win and a runner-up finish in recent starts, but two unplaced efforts either side temper enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and going, and drops in at 138 lb from stall 11 on a handy 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Treasure
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has placed at 7f on good twice recently; Patrick McGettigan's claim brings the weight down attractively, and a prominent racing style means he could slot in behind the pace battle and benefit if the front-runners overdo it.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 14 of 18 on our figures, Tokyo Treasure looks a tough proposition here, though he is at least fit from a run 11 days ago, has run over today's trip and going before, and his second last time out offers a crumb of hope.

runners_data.name: Dragon Of Malta
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type with blinkers and tongue-tie who finds good ground his best surface (8/15); amateur jockey Julian Pietropaolo adds risk in a competitive 18-runner field, and from OR 75 this looks a tough assignment without ideal positional luck.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dragon Of Malta at least arrives on a quick turnaround of 21 days and has run over today's trip and going before, but modest recent efforts and 135 lb from stall eight leave him with plenty to find against 17 rivals.

runners_data.name: Mehman
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer who wears a hood and has a modest record on similar going (3/15, no wins); form figures of 292300 suggest a horse who gets competitive without winning and the strong pace here may simply mean too much to do at the finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Mehman at least showed some consistency with a second and third in that sequence, though he has been unplaced in his two most recent outings; he has run over today's trip and going before, but a rating of 79 leaves him with ground to make up from stall five carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Red Hugh O'Donnell
runners_data.note: Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim helps on a wide-open handicap mark; hold-up profile with blinkers and tongue-tie, races best on good (11/15) and has a placed effort at this trip — needs the pace to collapse at the right moment for his late run to land.
runners_data.comment: Red Hugh O'Donnell finished eighth last time out and has been largely inconsistent in recent starts, winning one from his last five, and our rating ranks him near the foot of the field; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 21 days since his last run suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Thenandnow
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Harrington's powerful yard, won over 6f on soft and has placed twice on good — the step up to 7½f looks a logical progression for a horse who stays and sits prominently; Shane Foley retains the ride which is an important confidence sign.
runners_data.comment: Thenandnow shaped with promise when third two starts back and has experience of today's distance and going in her favour, but she needs to bounce back from a fifth last time out carrying a hefty 133 lb from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Cool Azul
runners_data.note: Won over 6f good most recently for A. Oliver, who is in flying form (4/19 over 14 days); this is a step up in trip to 7½f for the first time and the question is whether he truly stays when pressed hard early — if he does, he is the most likely leader to survive.
runners_data.comment: Cool Azul arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's going, with our rating of 85 marking him out as the top-ranked runner in the field; the main concern is a 38-day absence that leaves fitness a question mark.

runners_data.name: Dolly Hello
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with decent recent form (placed three times in last four starts over 7-8f on good); Seamie Heffernan rides but 35 days off the track and a mark of OR 72 means she needs everything to go right tactionally from a prominent draw position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked well adrift of the field on our figures, Dolly Hello faces a stiff task from stall 14 carrying 132 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a manageable 35-day break.

runners_data.name: Contrary To Law
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good for JP Murtagh and Ben Coen retains the ride — that combination has clocked 2/27 over 14 days showing they are not out of form; prominent style and solid form at 7f on good make this a course-and-distance profile that suits the expected race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Contrary To Law won two starts back and returns here on a 27-day break in good heart, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the 131 lb burden and draw 18 are the questions, but his recent winning form makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Perfect Base
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and is 61 days off the track — fitness queries are real; goes well on good (6/6 on similar going, placed twice at 7-8f) for Lupini but a distant tenth last time out means she needs significant improvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Perfect Base does at least have experience of today's distance and going, and a draw of two could be relevant; however, 61 days off the track and a tricky recent record — including a disqualification — leave questions to answer at 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Venetian Star
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner — this three-year-old has placed over 7f on good twice and Luke McAteer takes the ride; OR 74 is competitive but racing against two other pace horses at 7½f means this trip and this company will find her out if she can't dominate early.
runners_data.comment: Venetian Star returns after 40 days off winless in his last six starts, with two unplaced efforts sandwiching a second two starts back offering some encouragement, though his ranking of 12 of 18 and 128 lb from stall 15 suggest he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Sagasti
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Colin Keane and O'Callaghan, wears a visor, and has a placed record over 7f on good; hold-up profile that needs a truly run race to produce his best, and the strong pace scenario here suits him — Keane's tactical intelligence from the rear is a significant asset.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, Sagasti is hard to fancy, though a second two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement from stall ten off 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Mercurial
runners_data.note: Lupini's second runner here is a genuine prominent-type racer with a placed record at 6f and 7f on good and heavy — however, with three confirmed front-runners already dominating the pace map, he is very likely to find himself shuffled further back than his natural role demands, which will blunt his effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and fourth two starts back, Mercurial has shown enough consistency to be of interest from stall one, though a return from 79 days off and a winless recent run of form give pause for thought at 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Java Wood
runners_data.note: Won over 8f good and has placed at 6-8f across a range of going; a true hold-up horse by nature who finds himself mapped to midfield given the shape of this race — if he does get back to his natural position, the 8f wins suggest 7½f may be on the short side anyway.
runners_data.comment: Java Wood has finished seventh last time out and unplaced two starts back, and with our figures ranking him last of 18 runners, he is hard to fancy despite the experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old wearing a visor, trained by McGuinness who is in excellent form (5/28 over 14 days); a genuine hold-up horse who may end up further forward than preferred in this pace-heavy race — none of his last five runs have come on ground as good as today's, so the surface itself is a mild query.
runners_data.comment: Flaming Rib catches the eye on our ratings, ranked second of eighteen in the field, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions, returning after a sharp 15-day break; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts, including two poor efforts at the foot of the field.

races.paceDynamic: Spodo Komodo, Cool Azul, and Venetian Star are all confirmed front-runners in an 18-runner handicap over 7½f at Roscommon, making a strong, contested gallop from the outset virtually certain — none of these three will yield willingly, and the early sectionals should be genuinely testing. With pace distributed across the width of the field, the leaders will burn energy fighting for position through the first couple of furlongs, meaning the race is likely to be run at a true tempo that stretches the field and puts stamina firmly at a premium by the time they swing for home. This shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel just off the pace in the prominent-to-midfield berth — those who are not burning unnecessary fuel in the early stages but have enough tactical speed to pounce once the pace collapses in the final two furlongs — making the P-to-M profile the clear beneficiary. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate in their natural roles: Mercurial is a genuine prominent runner likely to be shuffled back, while Java Wood and Flaming Rib are true hold-up horses who will probably find themselves racing further forward than ideal given the competitive positioning early on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out and the pace collapses two furlongs from home, setting up a strong late run.
scenarios.body: Spodo Komodo, Cool Azul, and Venetian Star fight a war of attrition up front, leaving the stands-side rail littered with spent leaders as the race unravels; hold-up horses with genuine finishing pace — Summer Island and Sagasti — have enough clear road to motor home on the stands rail.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Sit-And-Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent racer settles just behind the hot pace and produces a well-timed challenge over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The blistering early fractions soften the leaders just enough for a horse tracking in third or fourth to have cover and kick decisively; Engines On, Thenandnow, or Contrary To Law — all capable of sitting in the slipstream — are ideally positioned to exploit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Cool Azul or Spodo Komodo — establishes a fractional advantage and the others crack first.
scenarios.body: Cool Azul, the only confirmed front-runner with a recent winning run over this trip and good ground, could dictate marginally off a soft enough gallop if one of the other leaders blinks; if the pace settles into something manageable rather than suicidal, a horse on the front end with tactical sense can simply outlast rivals who have been racing wide or with no cover.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Class Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively honest rather than truly fierce and the race becomes a stamina grind from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: In this shape a horse with superior class-to-weight ratio can simply grind through the pack as less-exposed rivals flatten; Summer Island and Earls — who have both shown consistent form in similar conditions and distances — are well-suited to a grinding finish where raw quality edges over positional tactics.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a three-way battle between Spodo Komodo, Cool Azul, and Venetian Star in the opening furlong — if all three refuse to cede the lead, the early fractions could be genuinely suicidal and will compromise all three runners' finishing prospects.

Summer Island is nine days fresh and Dylan Browne McMonagle has the mount — in an 18-runner field she will need a trouble-free run through the pack; if she gets a clear passage from the two-furlong pole her hold-up form here looks particularly dangerous.

Thenandnow is stepping up markedly in distance to 7½f for the first time — if she gets the prominent berth off a hot pace and this trip proves within her compass, the Shane Foley booking from a Harrington yard showing form is a significant red flag.

Contrary To Law's trainer JP Murtagh and jockey Ben Coen have teamed up with a recent winner over this exact trip and going — a horse who sits prominently and handles 7f on good well is worth tracking throughout.

Mercurial, Java Wood, and Flaming Rib are all racing outside their natural positional role given the pace demands of this field — monitor their early positioning; if any manages to slot into a comfortable spot rather than being shuffled around, their effective style-fit improves sharply.

races.name: District Speciality Coffee Maiden

runners_data.name: Ben Lomond
runners_data.note: A 6-year-old hold-up performer for Gerard Kyne returning after 337 days off; placed twice over 2m on good ground gives him stamina credentials, but such a lengthy absence is a significant concern and his redistribution to midfield masks his natural back-of-the-field style — he will likely race even further back than shown.

runners_data.name: Sea Celia's Star
runners_data.note: Luke Comer's 4-year-old has run just twice, finishing eighth on soft and tenth on good, with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish — the step up to 1m4f could expose those stamina limitations further.

runners_data.name: Sunny South West
runners_data.note: Edward Power's 6-year-old wears a hood and has been placed in nine of ten career starts including twice over today's trip on good ground — remarkably consistent prominent racer who has an excellent chance of securing a forward position in a race with few rivals wanting to be close to the pace.

runners_data.name: Almazann
runners_data.note: D K Weld's lightly raced 3-year-old finished second in both career runs on good ground, most recently over 1m2f, with Chris Hayes taking the ride — drops into a maiden having shaped with ability and should slot comfortably into a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Daily Wonder
runners_data.note: Debut runner for T G McCourt with no public form; going and style both Unknown, making any positional or tactical assessment speculative, though McCourt's recent trainer form (0/13 over 14 days) does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Magnum Cor
runners_data.note: JPO'Brien's 3-year-old is partnered by Dylan Browne McMonagle — a strong jockey booking — and finished fourth on his sole start on good ground; despite being a natural hold-up type, his high-profile partnership means he may be ridden more aggressively to find a better position than his true style would normally dictate.

runners_data.name: Michinaga
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's 3-year-old ran a disappointing ninth on debut on good ground with a noted tendency to fade; the style is Unknown but the finishing-fade flag makes 1m4f a concern rather than an obvious solution.

runners_data.name: One Cool County
runners_data.note: Finished sixth and ninth on good ground for P J F Murphy, last seen just 6 days ago — this is a genuinely held-up type who will likely find himself in midfield rather than at the rear given the volume of closers in this field, which tempers his chance of executing a true hold-up run.

runners_data.name: Purple Bandit
runners_data.note: Harrington's unraced 3-year-old wears a blindfold (blinkers) on debut — a notable headgear choice that can sharpen a green horse's concentration, and the yard has two winners from 32 runners over 14 days; entirely unknown quantity but worth monitoring in the parade ring.

runners_data.name: Swing Street
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this Richard O'Brien-trained 3-year-old who was sixth on debut over 1m2f on good — style is hold-up but there is little to go on, and at 57 days between runs the horse may need the outing.

runners_data.name: Teoest
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, trained by J S Bolger and ridden by Declan McDonogh — finished fourth and sixth over 1m2f, and the step up to 1m4f alongside uncontested lead privileges represents a significant upgrade in conditions that plays directly to his role.

runners_data.name: De Vega Queen
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the ride for J A Stack on this 3-year-old who has finished fifth, fourth and sixth; a hold-up type who will be crowded toward midfield by the volume of closers in the field, reducing her ability to produce the late run her style demands.

runners_data.name: My Girl Jersie
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's 3-year-old wears a hood and has run four times, posting 9-9-9-0 finishes mostly over shorter trips — multiple faders flag, shorter trip experience and redistribution out of her natural hold-up position all combine to make this a very difficult task over 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Possum
runners_data.note: Harrington's 3-year-old faded when eighth on debut over 1m2f on good ground; has had 76 days between runs and the finishing fade flag on a step up in trip is not encouraging — needs significant improvement to feature.

runners_data.name: Salamina
runners_data.note: JPO'Brien's 3-year-old has run just 4 days ago and posted back-to-back 11th-place finishes over 1m2f on good ground; the fades-in-finish flag and very recent run are both concerns, and Shay Wallace (7lb claim) is a significant drop in jockey quality relative to stablemate Magnum Cor.

runners_data.name: Venerini
runners_data.note: Michael Butler's 3-year-old has run twice — eighth and tenth — with a fade flag, and has been off 105 days; the apprentice partnership (Paddy Harnett, 5lb) and limited form make it difficult to assess, though the step to 1m4f could in theory suit a hold-up type if the stamina is present.

races.paceDynamic: Teoest is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner maiden, and with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, Declan McDonogh can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over 1m4f on good ground at Roscommon. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Ben Lomond, Magnum Cor, One Cool County, De Vega Queen, My Girl Jersie and others are all genuine closers, but the sheer number of hold-up horses means most will be racing closer to midfield than their natural style demands, compressing the pack behind Teoest. Sunny South West and Almazann are the likeliest to actually secure a prominent position just off the pace, giving them a meaningful tactical advantage over the genuine closers who cannot all settle as deep as they need. This race shape — a lone leader setting a measured pace with a congested midfield — strongly favours hold-up-mapped horses that can travel in midfield and produce a sustained run into the straight, and particularly prominent racers who can track the pace comfortably rather than being bottled up in a crowded pack. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can physically place at the rear, and among the redistrubuted horses, Magnum Cor (Dylan Browne McMonagle, JPO'Brien) and One Cool County are most likely to actually secure a forward position relative to the true backmarkers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Teoest Leads, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Teoest controls a steady pace and a prominent tracker sustains a clean run through the straight.
scenarios.body: Teoest sets a relaxed fractions-dictating gallop, and a horse sitting second or third — tracking without expending energy — has the clearest run and best jump on the field entering the final two furlongs. Sunny South West (twice second at the trip on good, headgear) and Almazann (twice placed on good, D K Weld) are ideally positioned to capitalise on this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that the midfield bunches, and one hold-up type finds clear daylight late to grind past a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: Teoest's controlled gallop sets up a slowly-run race that collapses into a sprint, but on 1m4f good ground the stamina-testing final furlong can reward a horse who has conserved energy through a congested midfield. Ben Lomond (6yo, 337 days off, stamina pedigree) or Swing Street could pick off tired rivals if they find a gap, though the redistributed closers face a trickier task than their true style would normally suggest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Sails Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Teoest's rivals fail to close and the steady pace is never truly challenged, allowing the front-runner to coast home unchallenged.
scenarios.body: At 1m4f with no pace pressure, Teoest can husband his reserves perfectly and quicken away from a field that is caught flat-footed after travelling in a bunch; Bolger-trained horses are capable of front-running wins when conditions suit and competition for the lead is absent. McDonogh riding to his own rhythm makes this a genuine possibility, particularly if the midfield fails to organise a timely challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed debutants — Purple Bandit or Daily Wonder — proves vastly superior on debut and overcomes positional uncertainty.
scenarios.body: With Unknown going style ratings for both debutants, either could be a smart individual that the market has underestimated, and first-time-out winners are not uncommon in Irish maidens from yards like Harrington or McCourt when a well-bred horse takes the eye in the paddock. However, the positional chaos of 16 runners and no established form makes this the least predictable and least likely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Sunny South West is the primary pace threat to Teoest's supremacy — if this consistent prominent racer tracks the leader closely for the full 1m4f and has energy in reserve at the two-furlong pole, she is well positioned to take this race given her record of nine placings in ten starts.

Almazann's booking of Chris Hayes for D K Weld is a high-profile combination in a race where the horse's prominent style and good-ground placed form make him a natural fit — watch for him to travel just off the pace and challenge from two furlongs out.

Dylan Browne McMonagle on Magnum Cor could ride aggressively to avoid being buried in the midfield cavalry charge — if he pushes forward early in a 16-runner field, the race shape could change and Teoest's easy lead would be disrupted.

Purple Bandit's debut blinkers application is a flag — if this horse is sharp from the gates and gets a clean run in a big field, first-time headgear combined with an unknown style profile means the horse could appear anywhere in the early stages and catch rivals off-guard.

With 16 runners and a very slow early pace expected, watch for traffic problems and scrimmaging in midfield at around the half-mile mark — horses like One Cool County and Ben Lomond, racing closer than their natural position, may find themselves blocked at a crucial stage.

races.name: Class Grass Handicap

runners_data.name: Catherine Magennis
runners_data.note: Placed twice from three runs on Good ground including a solid second over 12f, she races prominently and Seamie Heffernan's booking adds significant class to the partnership; the step up to 14f appears within range given those placed efforts and she is ideally positioned to stalk Out On Friday throughout.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of her last two starts, Catherine Magennis arrives here in good nick after 29 days off, with experience of today's trip and going working in her favour; third last time out and a runner-up two starts back, she looks the one to beat despite being yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Leggagh
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Soft and has placed form on Good, but a routine 16th on Good last time is a concern; Hannah Rafferty claims 10lb and the hold-up style means he needs something to go wrong ahead of him, though the long Roscommon straight at least gives closers a fighting chance.
runners_data.comment: Duke of Leggagh won one of his last five starts and tackles a trip and going he has already encountered, arriving here fresh on a 20-day break and carrying a weight our rating of 79 suggests he can handle; the risk is a run of unplaced efforts in more recent starts.

runners_data.name: Daonethatgotaway
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed twice in staying company, but his Good-ground record reads five from fifteen with no wins or places under today's conditions; the 7lb claimer Reese Holohan takes the ride and the horse needs the pace to truly collapse to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Daonethatgotaway showed a glimmer of potential with a win six starts back, but his last three runs have been well below that level; he has experience over today's trip and going, and a 17-day turnaround keeps him fresh, though the 140 lb is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Deralo Ir
runners_data.note: Beaten a long way back in two of his last three on Good, and despite placed efforts on Soft he looks to lack the pace to land this off a slow tempo; Robbie Colgan rides but the hold-up style makes him dependent on a scenario this race shape is unlikely to produce.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked well down on our figures, Deralo Ir is hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable 140 lb; a second four starts back is the sole encouragement, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, recent form makes him a tough sell.

runners_data.name: Lady Plimsoll
runners_data.note: Has placed three times in her last five including a third over 14f on Soft and a second over 16f at Stanmore; trainer M D O'Callaghan has two wins from 14 runners in the last fortnight and she holds genuine each-way claims given her comfort at this trip and her ability to race handily.
runners_data.comment: Consistent sort who has placed in four of her last five starts — third last time out and third two starts back, with a second three starts back — but Lady Plimsoll remains yet to win and her 140 lb burden may test her resolve here.

runners_data.name: Enchanted Lady
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield map because the rear is over-subscribed — her last five runs show five consecutive failures to place, largely over shorter trips; the step up to 14f could unlock improvement but her racing style is mismatched to a slow-tempo race where held-up horses struggle.
runners_data.comment: Enchanted Lady arrives on the back of a ninth last time out and has been winless in her last five starts, with a fifth three starts back the best of recent efforts; she has run over today's trip and going, but rated 11th of 18 she faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Summer Snow
runners_data.note: Three wins and four places from fifteen Good-ground runs suggest she handles conditions fine, but recent form shows a sequence of poor efforts including 17th and 15th; now wearing a tongue-tie and coming back from 11 days, this is a difficult assignment in an 18-runner handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Summer Snow arrives on an 11-day turnaround with going experience in her favour, and our rating of 77 marks her out as a leading danger; the chief concern is a sequence of disappointing finishes that offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Double Indian
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish and held-up in style, he is shifted into midfield on the map because of overcrowding at the rear; his last four all came on Good ground with zero wins or places from four attempts, and the tendency to fade under pressure is a serious concern at 14f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Double Indian arrives here 35 days fresh and with experience of today's trip and going, though a run of eighth, seventh and ninth gives little encouragement, and a hefty 138 lb is an additional burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Coulstys Way
runners_data.note: Placed third over 14f on Good recently with a Goodwood-style staying profile, and wearing first-time headgear that day; Jack Kearney claims 3lb and despite being a natural hold-up type squeezed to midfield, his course-distance form at this trip makes him the most interesting of the redistributed group if he can get closer to the pace than usual.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 12 of 18 here, Coulstys Way nevertheless showed ability with a third two starts back, though the unseating latest is a concern; she has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb is no light burden.

runners_data.name: Lily Parr
runners_data.note: Has placed four times but never won, primarily over shorter trips on Soft or Heavy; her Good-ground record is largely unsuccessful and she is a true hold-up horse shuffled to midfield by the numbers — the combination of unsuited going tendency and positional disadvantage makes this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lily Parr heads here 19 days after a sixth, carrying 135 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 72 offers some encouragement that better may be in her.

runners_data.name: Master Sydney
runners_data.note: His best form has come over extreme distances — third over 19f and fourth over 18f — but he has faded badly in the last two and is 10 days since his last run; a genuine hold-up stayer mapped to midfield, he is interesting only if the trip produces a stamina-test late on.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and drawn from a yard without a win in 27 attempts over the past fortnight, Master Sydney faces an uphill task, though her experience over today's trip and going and a quick ten-day turnaround at least suggest she arrives ready.

runners_data.name: Out On Friday
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who will dictate the entire shape of this race; at 10 years old his form figures have been modest but his ability to bowl along untouched at a Good-ground Roscommon makes him genuinely dangerous as a controlling force, and his placed second at 10f last year shows he can still produce a performance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 14 of 18 on our figures, Out On Friday makes for a tough sell; a second four starts back offers a rare crumb of comfort, and he does have experience over today's trip and going, returning after 18 days off carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Spy
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has won twice in the last five runs including over 16f on Good, but those wins came at Galway and Limerick over longer distances; a true hold-up horse remapped to midfield, his stamina is proven but he needs a test the slow pace is unlikely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Spy won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid platform, though he carries 131 lb and his record shows inconsistency in recent starts, with two sixths alongside the better efforts.

runners_data.name: Chopsticks
runners_data.note: Wearing a tongue-tie and hood, he has placed at 12f on Good and won at 12f on Stanmore; trainer John C McConnell has three winners from 28 runners recently and the apprentice Nathan Crosse rides, but his Good-ground record over this sort of trip shows a ceiling that makes him an each-way outsider at best.
runners_data.comment: Chopsticks has struggled badly in his last three starts, finishing unplaced twice and ninth, and he ranks 15th of 18 on our figures — hard to fancy despite being winless in recent starts, experience over today's trip and going offering slim comfort.

runners_data.name: Fianna
runners_data.note: 118 days since last run is a significant flag, and wearing a tongue-tie and hood; placed at 12f-13f on Good ground in his last five, he stays adequately but the long absence, combined with being a hold-up horse in a race where that style is disadvantaged, makes this a speculative return.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 13 of 18 on our figures, Fianna faces a stiff ask on return from a 118-day absence, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her third three starts back shows she can find the frame.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Most interesting runner at the bottom of the weights — won over 9f and placed third at the same trip in his last five, and his OR of 50 gives him a massive weight advantage; the question is solely whether 14f is within his stamina range, and if it is, the combination of low weight and improving profile makes him a live player in a scenario where pace collapses.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 17 of 18 on our figures, Yquem makes for a tough sell despite a win three starts back and a third two starts back; she has run over today's trip and going before, but a return to that level looks required.

runners_data.name: Autocrat
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and breastplate, has faded in the finish flag attached, and his last fifteen Good-ground runs show just four placed efforts and no wins; a hold-up horse in a slow-pace race is the worst-case scenario for this profile and the fading tendency compounds that concern.
runners_data.comment: Autocrat landed a win six starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, so the ingredients are there for a revival after 29 days off; the concern is that he has been out of the frame in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Piatra Neamt
runners_data.note: Three consecutive failures to finish in the frame including a dismal 18th, and wears a hood; his Good-ground record is poor and the fading-in-finish tag is concerning over 14f; the low weight of 119lbs is the only mildly positive angle but the overall profile suggests he is likely to struggle throughout.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Piatra Neamt makes for a difficult proposition, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a handy 13-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Out On Friday is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field over 1m4f at Roscommon on Good ground, and with no genuine rival willing to chase them down early, they are set to dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front. This creates a race that will be run at a measured, sustainable tempo — unlikely to overly tax the leader and unlikely to generate a truly searching test for the closers. The massive hold-up contingent — including Catherine Magennis and Lady Plimsoll who will seek to race prominently — will face a compressed midfield, leaving those at the back with ground to make up against a pace that may never truly collapse. Tactically, this race shape strongly favours horses who can settle just off Out On Friday in the prominent or stalking positions, as they will control their own fate without surrendering ground to a slowly-run contest; genuine hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged here. The field contains far more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear in their natural position, with Enchanted Lady, Double Indian, Lily Parr, Coulstys Way, Master Sydney and others all redistributed to midfield — of these, Enchanted Lady and Coulstys Way are most likely to actually secure a position closer to the pace given their recent form and natural tendency to travel up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Out On Friday bowls along uncontested and sets a steady, honest gallop that nobody seriously challenges.
scenarios.body: Out On Friday sets their own terms through the early and middle stages, and the prominent stalkers who have tracked closest — Catherine Magennis, Lady Plimsoll — arrive at the straight with the most to give; the hold-up horses face a long, flat run-in having given away too much ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting second or third off Out On Friday times their move perfectly turning for home and has enough class to overhaul the leader.
scenarios.body: The compressed pace means little change in the order until the straight, where a well-placed stalker with reserves left kicks past a tiring leader; horses who naturally want to be on the pace but have been held slightly off it are ideally situated.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is just strong enough to soften Out On Friday inside the final two furlongs and a horse tracking from midfield delivers a late surge.
scenarios.body: A horse like Duke Of Leggagh or Coulstys Way — who have won at shorter distances and can quicken when a gap opens — would benefit from any fractional increase in tempo that unwinds the leaders; the long Roscommon straight gives a sustained finisher a fighting chance if the pace has been honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Genuinely Slow Pace Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If Out On Friday crawls and the field bunches chaotically, turning the race into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners jostling in a small space at the end of a truly dawdling contest, positional luck and a clear run become decisive; horses stuck wide or blocked in a wall of rivals are eliminated regardless of ability.

watchPoints.text: Out On Friday — watch whether they are allowed to bowl clear uncontested or whether Catherine Magennis or Lady Plimsoll push up to pressurise; the pace they set in the first half-mile will define every scenario.
Coulstys Way — monitor where Jack Kearney settles in the early stages; if he can get closer to the pace than his natural hold-up style suggests, his 14f placed form becomes genuinely relevant.

Duke Of Leggagh — last-time 16th should not be ignored but the 10lb claim from Hannah Rafferty is meaningful in a low-grade handicap; watch whether he can find a position closer to midfield than the rear given the congestion.

Yquem — the key question to resolve before betting is stamina; if market support suggests connections believe 14f is within range, his combination of low weight, improving profile and recent win makes him one to monitor on the drift or steam.
Fianna — 118 days off is the longest absence in the field; watch for any significant market move that would suggest the stable believes the horse is fully ready to do themselves justice on return.
